response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.observstation, COUNT(t.telescregistry) AS cnt FROM observatories o LEFT JOIN telescopes t ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY o.observstation), s AS (SELECT observstation, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM telescopes) AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT observstation, cnt, share, share - (SELECT AVG(share) FROM s) AS diff FROM s), f AS (SELECT observstation, cnt, share, diff, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY diff DESC) AS rk FROM a WHERE share > (SELECT AVG(share) FROM s)) SELECT observstation, cnt AS telescope_count, share, diff AS share_above_average FROM f WHERE rk <= 10 ORDER BY diff DESC, observstation

assumptions.assumption: All rows in the observatories table count as observatories, including any with zero telescopes. Those stations get a count of 0 and are part of the average share, which is then 1/(number of observatories).
Share is the observatory's telescope count divided by the total number of rows in telescopes. Ties with the 10th row are kept by using RANK() on the difference.

alternatives.interpretation: Only observatories that have at least one telescope are counted, so the average share is taken over those stations only.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT observstation, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM telescopes GROUP BY observstation), s AS (SELECT observstation, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM telescopes) AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT observstation, cnt, share, share - (SELECT AVG(share) FROM s) AS diff FROM s), f AS (SELECT observstation, cnt, share, diff, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY diff DESC) AS rk FROM a WHERE share > (SELECT AVG(share) FROM s)) SELECT observstation, cnt AS telescope_count, share, diff AS share_above_average FROM f WHERE rk <= 10 ORDER BY diff DESC, observstation
